value.overview: The Mexican Whip-poor-will (Antrostomus arizonae) is a nightjar recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from nightjar shape, cryptic mottled plumage, broad wings, and repeated whip-poor-will style song at dusk or night. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 4 state or DC summaries, including AZ, CA, NM, TX. It is most associated with Forests:  Mesoamerican Pine-Oak and Forests:  Mesoamerican Highland, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Mexican Whip-poor-will belongs to the family Nightjars and Allies in the order Caprimulgiformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for nightjar shape, cryptic mottled plumage, broad wings, and repeated whip-poor-will style song at dusk or night. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
